evidence_quotes:
Where the instruction “clean” appears in a procedure, you must use drycleaning solvent (Appendix C,
Item 18) to clean grease or oil from metal parts.
Clean parts with drycleaning solvent (SD), type II, or equivalent.
statements.reason: The general cleaning instruction specifies drycleaning solvent for grease or oil on metal parts, and the lubrication instruction specifies type II or equivalent for parts.
statements.statement: The cleaning agent generally specified for grease or oil on metal parts is drycleaning solvent (SD), type II, or equivalent.

evidence_quotes: Do not clean CDR valve with solvent.
statements.reason: The CDR valve instruction prohibits cleaning it with solvent.
statements.statement: Drycleaning solvent (SD), type II, or equivalent must not be used to clean the CDR valve.

evidence_quotes:
Do not clean CDR valve with solvent.
This will damage the diaphragm in-
side the CDR valve.
statements.reason: The caution explicitly states this consequence.
statements.statement: Cleaning the CDR valve with solvent will damage the diaphragm inside the CDR valve.

evidence_quotes:
Wiping with a rag
is the only authorized method of
cleaning.

Remove and wipe off the CDR valve
and hoses with a rag.
statements.reason: The instruction makes rag wiping the only authorized cleaning method and directs it for the valve and hoses.
statements.statement: The authorized CDR valve cleaning method is to wipe the CDR valve and the CDR valve hoses with a rag only.
